title: Choose the visual world
question: Systems thinker with personality. The roll assigned the Assembly Manual. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Assembly Manual
options.lineage: Wordless building-set and flat-pack instruction booklets
options.thesis: Jarod builds the parts other teams assemble products from; the site is the instruction booklet.
materials: isometric line drawing on your monogram's 60° grid
options.viewport: A full-width Step 1 page: name as the set title with an "18+" box badge (18 years), a parts box holding the bio pills as labeled pieces, CTAs as the next step, and the JT monogram exploded into isometric parts that slide together and click on load.
options.risk: Could tip toward toy and cost seniority if drawn cartoonish; it has to stay technically precise.

raised.raise: Structure is the only ornament: every graphic on the page is a real part, step or assembly line, nothing decorative.
One identical parts-callout module repeats on every step, so the system reads as a ruler.
Full saturation is reserved for the decisive beat: the click when the monogram locks together.
Every step keeps the same grid and part scale, so progress down the page reads like turning pages.

options.label: Standards Manual
options.thesis: The site is Jarod's own standards manual, the ancestor of every design system he has founded.
options.viewport: A black band across the top with the name set in it, a spec sheet below with the role, three colored bullets for the pillars, and the bio and CTAs set like manual body copy.
options.risk: Familiar to designers (the reissued manual is a staple) and can read corporate or cold, which you flagged.

options.label: Living Type Specimen
options.thesis: Your name is the specimen; drag one axis and the whole page re-tokens live.
options.viewport: The name fills the width; a slider under it morphs weight and width live while a readout counts token values, previewing Remix.
options.case: Engineers will love it and it proves the tokens directly; loses on recruiter clarity and personality.
options.risk: Reads as a font demo, not a person, and can feel cold.

options.label: Paper Automaton
options.thesis: Humble parts and linkages produce surprising motion: systems with personality, literally.
options.viewport: A cut-paper machine beside the name; turning its crank (drag or scroll) drives linkages that raise the three pillars as figures.
options.case: Strongest personality on the table; loses on clarity and costs real illustration work.
options.risk: Gimmick risk: a recruiter has to play with it to get it.

options.label: Exposed Binding
options.thesis: Nothing hidden: the stitching that holds it together is the ornament.
options.viewport: A flat-open book with a stitched spine as navigation.
options.case: Too close to Backstage and too quiet; loses both axes.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Stats as a row of needles leaning into the red.
options.viewport: Four meters for the four stats.
options.case: Recruiters don't identify with a mixing desk; clarity drops.
options.kept: Identical repeated units as a ruler.

options.label: Manga Page
options.thesis: The career as panels with speed lines.
options.viewport: Panels with the name breaking the gutter.
options.case: Personality without the systems; clarity drops.
options.kept: Reserve the solid beat for one decisive moment.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Career stages as plates of one plant.
options.case: Soft and literary; loses both axes.
options.kept: Fixed scale and registration across every plate.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Big name, short bio, dark ground, one accent, work list below, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name huge at left, role and bio beneath, socials, a quiet animated field (like aarronwalter.com).
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the best of the competition by design.
